REASONING

Content pillar: service_highlight with neighborhood_authority undertone — the safety model is the service story.

Today is April 6. National Dog Bite Prevention Week starts April 12 — six days out. The priority action asks for two posts this week that connect the double-leash and individual-walk model to that week. That means I can and should write teaser/lead-up content now, positioning the safety message ahead of the week, but I cannot frame it as "it's here" or "this week" as if the event is live today.

The ask is for two posts. I'll write both: one publishable today (April 6) as a warm lead-in that earns trust through specifics, and one timed for April 12 or later when the week is actually live — clearly labeled so the founder knows which to post when.

Emotion target: trust, curiosity, mild surprise — "I didn't know that, I should save this."
Angle that feels like news, not marketing: leaning into a specific, concrete question about dog bite risk that reframes individual walks as a safety default, not a luxury.
Save/share trigger: a stat or framing that makes an attentive dog owner think "my vet should know this" or "I should send this to my dog-walking group chat."

For Post 1 (publishable April 6): plant the safety seed without forcing the event date. Use a grounded question or stat as the hook. Frame individual walks and double leash as the operational standard.

For Post 2 (publishable April 12–18, when the week is live): more direct tie-in, stat-forward, drives saves.

---

INSTAGRAM_POST_COPY (POST 1 — publish April 6):

Most dog bites happen during leash interactions with unfamiliar dogs.

It's one reason we walk dogs individually and always use a double leash. Not as an add-on. Just how we do it — since 2011.

Ahead of National Dog Bite Prevention Week (April 12–18), we'll be sharing more about why the walk setup matters as much as the walker.

DM us if you're looking for a consistent walker in Williamsburg or Greenpoint.

#WilliamsburgDogs #DogSafety #NotTheRug

---

CONTENT_ANGLE (POST 1):

This post uses the six-day runway before National Dog Bite Prevention Week to plant a safety credential without overclaiming. The hook leads with a specific, checkable fact about bite risk that reframes the double-leash and individual-walk model as a practical safety standard — not a premium tier. The teaser language ("we'll be sharing more") creates a reason to follow the account through the week and signals to new leads that this business thinks operationally, not just commercially. The local CTA keeps acquisition intent present without hard-selling.

---

INSTAGRAM_POST_COPY (POST 2 — publish April 12 or during April 12–18):

Most dog bites involve a dog the victim knows — and leash tension between unfamiliar dogs is one of the most common triggers.

This is National Dog Bite Prevention Week. We think about it as a reminder of why individual walks exist.

One dog. One walker. Double leash. GPS on every walk. Same team, same routes, dogs who know their walker.

That's the setup we've run since 2011. Not a feature. Just the job.

DM us to get started in Williamsburg or Greenpoint.

#DogBitePreventionWeek #WilliamsburgDogs #NotTheRug

---

CONTENT_ANGLE (POST 2):

This post goes live when the awareness week is actually live, converting the cultural moment into a specific, credible service proof point. The stat in the opener is designed to stop the scroll and earn a save from attentive dog owners — the kind who research before hiring and share useful safety content with other owners. By listing the operational specifics (individual walks, double leash, GPS, consistent team) in plain language rather than as marketing claims, the post positions Not The Rug as a business that was already doing this work long before it became content fodder. The "not a feature, just the job" framing is the key trust signal: it rejects hype while asserting quiet confidence.
